tasks.title: Peak at the wrong logging rate
tasks.statement: Betaflight: PID loop **{fp} Hz**, `blackbox_sample_rate = 1/{d}`. The spectrum was computed with `fs = {fp}` (the divider was forgotten) and showed a peak at **{fo} Hz**. At what frequency is the peak actually, in Hz?
tasks.solution: The true logging rate is fs = f_PID / d. Every frequency in the spectrum is scaled by fs_used / fs_true = d, so f = f_observed / d. One rule fixes it: take fs from the log timestamps, not from the settings.

tasks.title: Where a peak above Nyquist folds to
tasks.statement: The gyro was logged at **{fs} Hz** (with no anti-aliasing before logging). The mechanics have a vibration at **{f} Hz**. At what frequency will it appear in the spectrum of this log, in Hz?
tasks.solution: A component f sampled at fs appears at |f − k·fs|, where k is the integer nearest to f/fs; the result always lies in 0…fs/2. If f < fs/2, the peak stays where it is. The module's example: 250 Hz at 400 Hz → 150 Hz.

tasks.title: Step overshoot
tasks.statement: The roll setpoint went from **{b} °/s** to **{s} °/s**. After the step the gyro peaked at **{p} °/s**, then settled. Find the overshoot as a % of the step size.
tasks.solution: Normalize the response to the step: r = (gyro − base)/(target − base). Overshoot = (max r − 1)·100 = (peak − target)/(target − base)·100. Dividing by target instead of by the step is a common mistake when the step does not start from zero.
